You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The structure is described in the orthorhombic space group Imm2, space-group number 44, with Hall symbol I 2 -2, using fractional atomic coordinates. The input cell is not the conventional Imm2 cell: it has lattice parameters a = 4.853969 Å, b = 6.5051485 Å, c = 6.5051485 Å, α = 97.58547794999998°, β = 111.90611431999999°, and γ = 68.09388568°. This original cell contains 14 atoms with the declared input composition Dy1 Ti1 Fe11 C1. The standard and input fractional frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the origin shift s is (0, 0, 0) and the matrix P has rows (1.0, 0.5, -0.5), (1.4903476486807066e-17, -0.49999999999999994, -0.5), and (1.4903476486807066e-17, 0.49999999999999994, -0.5). Thus the first standard coordinate is q1_input + 0.5 q2_input - 0.5 q3_input, while the second and third standard coordinates are, up to the stated near-zero numerical terms of order 1.49e-17, -0.5 q2_input - 0.5 q3_input and 0.5 q2_input - 0.5 q3_input, respectively. Coordinate values are rounded to six digits, and no precision corrections are required.

In the standard Imm2 description, dysprosium occupies the 2a orbit with coordinate relation (0, 0, z); its independent representative is (0, 0, 0.992567), so the independent positional parameter is z = 0.992567 and the orbit has multiplicity 2. Titanium also occupies a 2a orbit of the same form, but with an independent z parameter of 0.36643500000000007, represented by (0, 0, 0.36643500000000007). These two inequivalent 2a sites place Dy and Ti separately along the same x = 0, y = 0 line at different heights along z.

Iron is distributed over five independent orbits. One Fe 2b orbit follows (0, 1/2, z) with representative (0, 0.5, 0.275266), hence z = 0.275266 and multiplicity 2. A second, inequivalent Fe 2b orbit has the same coordinate relation but representative (0, 0.5, 0.722596), corresponding to z = 0.722596. A fourfold Fe orbit on Wyckoff position 4d follows (0, y, z), with representative (0, 0.28000650000000005, 0.5021995), so its independent parameters are y = 0.28000650000000005 and z = 0.5021995. The most general iron sublattice is the 8e orbit with coordinate relation (x, y, z), represented by (0.24947350000000013, 0.24844750000000015, 0.7492905); its three independent coordinates are x = 0.24947350000000013, y = 0.24844750000000015, and z = 0.7492905, with multiplicity 8. Another Fe 2a orbit lies on (0, 0, z) with representative (0, 0, 0.643268), giving z = 0.643268. Finally, a second independent Fe 4d orbit follows (0, y, z) with representative (0, 0.35866599999999993, 0.999973), so y = 0.35866599999999993 and z = 0.999973.

Carbon occupies a 2b orbit with coordinate relation (0, 1/2, z), represented by (0, 0.5, 0.49836); its independent parameter is z = 0.49836 and its multiplicity is 2. Together, the independent sublattices are therefore Dy on 2a, Ti on a distinct 2a, Fe on two distinct 2b orbits, two distinct 4d orbits, one 8e orbit, and one additional 2a orbit, and C on 2b. The body-centered Imm2 symmetry and the stated Wyckoff relations generate the full periodic arrangement from these independent representatives while preserving the original nonstandard input cell through the specified transformation.
